adjudicated.jp: 自分が死を肯定できるとは思えない。
adjudicated.en: I don't think I would be able to consent to my own death.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that he cannot imagine affirming or accepting death. The English narrows the abstraction specifically to his own death.

adjudicated.jp: 生存への本能は強い方だ。
adjudicated.en: The instinct to exist is very strong.
adjudicated.assessment: 生存への本能 is the established concept 'survival instinct.' 'Instinct to exist' is an awkward literal paraphrase.

adjudicated.jp: 砂漠の虫みたいに、しぶといはず。
adjudicated.en: As tenacious, likely, as an insect in the desert.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: それに、霧が向けてくる憎悪が、俺にははかりかねた。
adjudicated.en: Besides, the hatred that came from Kiri was something I didn't really know what to do with.
adjudicated.assessment: はかりかねた means that he could not fathom or gauge the hatred directed at him. The English instead says he did not know how to respond to or handle it.

The repeated のに is concessive: even though there is nothing but despair. 'So' makes despair the cause of the adjoining obligation and reverses the relation.

adjudicated.jp: 笑っていかねばならないのに。
adjudicated.assessment: 笑っていかねばならない means that he nevertheless must go on smiling. The English reduces this sustained stance to merely laughing and adds 'just.'

comments: Likely exactly what happened at the end of the Misato route of Downfall -GHS

adjudicated.jp: 視界の外、何かが、肉に、食いこんだ。
adjudicated.en: Out of sight... something had... eaten down... into flesh.
comments: Catfight? See CCA0017A, someone likes to bite indeed. See CCA0003 as well -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 食いこむ means that something bites or digs into flesh. The English literalizes the verb as eating and uses past perfect for the immediate event.
